subject: Biotechnology
title: Subunit and Recombinant Vaccines
description: A quick win: understand Subunit and Recombinant Vaccines.

hook.text: Why inject a whole virus when one protein is enough? Subunit vaccines use just the piece that matters.

buildup.text: The hepatitis B vaccine was the first recombinant vaccine — yeast cells produce the surface antigen protein.

discovery.text: Novavax's COVID vaccine uses spike proteins grown in insect cells — no virus, no mRNA, just the purified protein.

twist.text: Pure proteins are weak immunogens alone — adjuvants like aluminum salts or saponins boost the immune response.

climax.text: Shingrix uses a recombinant glycoprotein with AS01B adjuvant — over 90% effective even in elderly patients.

punchline.text: One protein plus an adjuvant — subunit vaccines are safe and precise.

quiz.question: Why do subunit vaccines need adjuvants?
options: Adjuvants stabilize the protein during storage
Purified proteins alone provoke a weak immune response that adjuvants amplify
Adjuvants convert the protein into mRNA for better delivery
